context.significance: The story combines an unverified, intelligence-sourced allegation of a radiological attack on the US capital with the first renewed kinetic exchanges between the US and Iran after a two-month lull. It shows how quickly a fragile pause in Gulf hostilities can unravel, and how threat reporting, official rhetoric, and denials can feed escalation before facts are established. Dirty bomb fears also highlight a long-standing gap between the public's perception of radiological weapons and their actual effects, which are mainly disruption and contamination rather than mass casualties.
